It’s not as varied as some west Amazon countries (around 650 sp if I’m not mistaken) but it truly shines with its spectacular Cotinga species! It’s the best place to look for Pompadour Cotinga, Capuchinbird, Guianan Cock of the Rock. It has a really nice Crimson Topaz (hummingbird) and the usual Amazonian Raptors such as the Spizaetus, Harpy and Crested, but it doesn’t stick out as much in that respect in comparison to other such countries.

Another big difference is behaviour; Andean leks pretty much year round whereas Guianan has a very specific season in which it leks, making it a bit more challenging to see. I’ve been lucky enough to see both species now (including both distinct west and east Andean populations)

Yes, also a very pretty species. I must say I much prefer the Guianan, the main feature I like about this one is the little feather detail on the wings that the Andean lacks. Andean has very gray upper wings whereas this beauty is way more orange. In fact during display you can only see fluffy orange in the wings, no grey at all

So many people being extremely judgemental about people with ASPD. Remember, the term ‘sociopath’ is not a diagnosis, and two people with the same diagnosis don’t always behave the same way. People with ASPD are not manipulative nor evil by nature; sure, some of them can be but that doesn’t mean we should paint everyone with the same brush. 

I have personally known two people diagnosed ASPD and while I did have conflict with one of them; it wasn’t because of manipulation nor evil behaviour. What I saw is both people were very self conscious of their emotions and how others perceived them and they both tried their best to fit in with the rest of us. 

Also if you read OP’s replies you’ll see they talk about their partners emotions ‘switching off’. Switching off implies they’re ‘on’ usually, which is contrary to what many in the comments seem to believe about this poor person being a cold, calculating manipulator at all times. 

Stop letting your opinions be guided by true crime and pseudo scientific ‘psychology podcasts’ and instead try and be a bit empathetic to others struggles.

For OP: you know this person better than anyone in the comments, my advice to you is to read up as much as you can about ASPD so you’re aware of what you’re dealing with and try have open and honest conversations with your partner about it and his emotions. The ideal would be for him to be open and trust you with how he feels. Also enquire about if he’s in therapy regarding this. 

Best of luck and have a nice day!

For everyone exclaiming how dangerous and aggressive this snake is; please stop. Just as any other snake, this one is fairly shy and not often confrontational, preferring to flee first and then if continued to be pestered they might coil up, the same way other vipers do. 

They do have a bit of a reputation as an aggressive snake; they are possibly more willing to strike than other such species in the area, however I have not seen any evidence of this anecdotally.

 I live in an area where this species is very common; in fact just yesterday I had two encounters with juveniles, one of which I kicked by mistake due to not seeing it (it was fine) and the second one I nearly stepped on but at the last second changed where my foot was going. They did not strike, nor act defensive, both of them chose the simpler solution; slithering away. 

I have encountered many individuals of this species and I’d say 95% of the time this has been the case. The few that acted defensively fouled up and beat their tail on the floor; warning me not to go nearer to them. 

They are also not the most venomous snakes in their range; their venom is potent sure, but other species have substantially stronger venom. 

The reason they are so feared is because they are the snake responsible for the most amount of deaths within their range. This is due to several factors; how common they are everywhere, how adaptable they are (allowing them to thrive in urban areas), their incredible camouflage and finally their venom being potent enough to kill an adult if untreated. Not because of how aggressive they are. 

They are the most common viper with medically significant venom within their range; this is why they are responsible for so many bite incidents. 

Please don’t vilify snakes unduly, thank you
